lawyer: AFM Mesbahuddin with Khandakar Diliruzzaman, Advocates—For the Petitioner.
parties:
Rafiqul Islam (Md) alias Syeed ---------- Petitioner
Vs. 
Abul Kalam Azad Khan and another ------------- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued by this Court on 24-9-2003 upon an application filed by the petitioner under section 115(1) of the code of civil procedure against the impugned judgment and order dated 30-6-2003 passed by Joint District Judge, Second Court, Barguna in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 1 of 2003 allowing the appeal by reversing those dated 13-11-2002 passed by Senior Assistant Judge, Barguna Sadar in Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 2001. 

 2. The relevant facts for disposal of the case, in a nutshell, are that the petitioner purchased the suit shop room measuring two decimals of land thereof from one Abdul Latif Khan, the father and father-in- law of both the opposite parties on 5-4-1998 by a registered sale deed at the cost of Taka 10,000 [ten thousand]. Having taken possession of the shop room the petitioner started getting prepared for extension of the shop while opposite party No.1, third son of the vendor, forcibly entered the suit room on 9-4-1998 at night and began to live therein along with opposite party No. 2. This incident was informed to the vendor and local elites who asked them to vacate the suit room to which opposite party No.1 gave an undertaking to vacate the same by 22-12-1998 or to pay an amount of Taka 18,000 as price of the shop room including cost of construction of the boundary wall. But the opposite parties neither paid the aforesaid money nor vacated the shop room, hence the suit. 

 4. Thereafter, opposite party No.1 presented Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 2001 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure stating that he came to know about the ex-parte decree on 1-1-2001 and the reasons shown by him is that he could not take step because of his ailment. In support of this plea he submitted some medical documents at the time of rendering evidence before the court below. 

 5. Upon hearing the parties, perusing the medical documents and evidence, the Senior Assistant Judge, Barguna by his order dated 13-11-2002 rejected the miscellaneous case. Against which the opposite party No. 1 preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 1 of 2003 before the learned District Judge, Barguna. Ultimately the said miscellaneous appeal was heard by the learned Joint District Judge and allowed the same setting aside the order of Senior Assistant Judge dated 13-11-2002. Hence, the instant Rule came into light at the instant of the petitioner. 

 6. Mr Khandakar Diliruzzaman, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner contends that the application under order IX Rule 13 filed by the opposite party No.1 was barred by limitation under Article 164 of the Limitation Act. Having found no cogent reason with regard to taking no steps by the opposite parties in the suit on the date fixed, the trial court rightly and lawfully dismissed the miscellaneous case but the Appellate Court below committed an error of law resulting in the decision occasioning failure of justice in setting aside the ex-parte decree, is liable to be set-aside. He further contends that the grounds taken by the petitioner in disposing the miscellaneous case were referred to the decision given by the Appellate Court merely allowing cost, is not enough to set-aside the decree which caused failure of justice and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set-aside. 

 8. Heard the submissions of learned Advocate for the petitioner, perused the application, judgments and orders of both the courts below and other connected documents wherefrom it transpires that a title suit was filed by the present petitioner as plaintiff for a decree of ejectment from semi pacca shop room. The opposite party No.1 as defendant No.1 appeared in the said title suit and took several adjournments for filing written statement. After a while he showed no interest to take steps on the dates fixed in the suit for filing written statement. The trial court had given him ample opportunities to contest the case by filing written statement but he failed to prevail such opportunity. Thereafter, the suit was decreed ex-parte on 25-4-2000. After a long time of the ex-parte decree he preferred a miscellaneous appeal before the learned Sessions Judge reasoning that he could not take proper steps due to his ailment by submitting medical certificates issued by the doctor who did not come forward to support the medical certificates issued by him. It has further revealed that the ex-parte decree was made on 25-4-2000 and the opposite party No.1 allegedly came to know about this ex-parte decree on 1-1-2001, around eight months he was silent in taking any steps against ex-parte decree by showing reasonable explanation. Even then he did not show anything about his engaged lawyer who ought to have informed him with regard to the ex-parte decree. 

 9. Supporting inordinate delay of taking steps he failed to produce evidence in the miscellaneous case. It appears from the judgment of Appellate Court below that he had been suffering from fever which turned into ulcer and rheumatic diseases. Such diseases were not supposed to make him unable to proceed with the case brought against him by the present petitioner and he could have scope to proceed with the case by suffering from such diseases. Learned judge of the Appellate Court below before taking final decision mentioned that the opposite party having appeared the case took adjournments for filing written statement but subsequently why did not take any steps next day i.e on 29-2-2000. Such views he expressed are the grounds of the petitioner but he did not consider it in favour of the petitioner. Moreover, as per Article 164 of the Limitation Act, the application for setting aside the ex-parte decree was to be filed within thirty days to be counted from the date of judgment and decree or when the applicant has knowledge of the decree if failed there must be a proper explanation for condonation of delay under Limitation Act which was not rendered by the opposite party and he could not have any scope to say that he had no knowledge about the ex-parte decree because he entered appearance in the suit after getting summons from the trial court and he would not know the subsequent fixed dates, is fettered from truthfulness.
